summary: Arctic Village Airport serves the remote Gwich'in Athabascan community of Arctic Village in northeastern Alaska, situated well above the Arctic Circle at the eastern edge of the Brooks Range. As a gravel-strip facility handling only small commuter and bush aircraft, it functions as the community's sole year-round transportation link to the outside world, since no roads connect the village to the rest of Alaska. The airport is essential for shipping in supplies, mail, and medical evacuations for the roughly 150 residents of this isolated settlement.

A: The airport is primarily served by regional bush carriers such as Warbelow's Air Ventures and Wright Air Service, operating scheduled flights to and from Fairbanks.
